policy_title: Bring privatised utilities into public ownership
stated: Immediately bring railways, water companies, and the Big 5 retail energy companies back into public ownership through public investment, to serve the public rather than shareholders.

source.quote: We commit to immediately bringing the railways, the water companies and the Big 5 retail energy companies back into public ownership. Public investment would buy equity in these public utilities, ensuring they are run to serve us all, rather than to increase the wealth of shareholders.

bearing_set.reason: Public ownership of retail energy companies and water companies would directly affect household energy bills and water bills — explicit O2 indicators — via pricing decisions no longer driven by shareholder returns; rail fares also affect real disposable income.

Water company ownership structure directly bears on water quality (an explicit O6 indicator) and investment in sewage/environmental standards; public ownership of energy retailers could materially affect the decarbonisation/emissions trajectory.

Acquiring railways, water companies, and five major energy retailers requires very large-scale public expenditure (or borrowing) for compensation, with a material and contested effect on debt sustainability.

Shifting ownership and control of key infrastructure sectors affects investment levels, efficiency, and productivity in ways that are genuinely contested between nationalisation advocates and opponents — a real, non-negligible effect on aggregate living standards.

membership_note: Four fundamentals carry real non-negligible verdicts: consumer prices for essentials (O2), environmental investment incentives especially in water (O6), the fiscal cost of acquisition (O12), and long-run productivity/investment in infrastructure (O13). O4 (workers' conditions) and O14 (inequality) are plausible but the mechanisms are secondary and subsumed within O2 and O13 at this stage.
